meta.tagline: Portland general contractor since 1996 · results + 6-month roadmap
meta.focus: Wins · long-tail footprint built · case for 6 more months at same budget targeting service × suburb matrix
meta.data_window: Local Dominator Feb 27 – May 5 2026 (169-cell grid · 8 queries; clean scan window) · GSC Dec 12 2025 – Jun 1 2026 (cmdesigns.net, siteOwner) · DataForSEO Labs ranked-keywords + Google Ads volumes + fresh Maps grid scan 2026-06-02 · live site crawl 2026-06-01 · Asana CMD-Tier 2 · HQDM engagement start 2026-03-12

tldr: Twelve weeks in, the foundation is proven and the brand is owned. cmdesigns.net now ranks #1 organically for its brand name and the content engine is demonstrably working: of the 10 blog posts shipped, three already rank on page 1 of Google (walk-in shower permits #7, insurance rebuilds #6, rebuild timeline #9), and the ADA walk-in-shower guide alone pulls a cluster of 44 distinct search queries. GSC impressions over the engagement window are up +112% (1,940 → 4,116), 186 brand-new queries found the site this quarter, and the brand keyword "cm&d" recovered from position 22.1 → 7.8. On Maps, the brand queries hold a broad top-3 footprint and full-grid top-10 coverage (169/169 cells) on the primary query at the last clean reading, and the most recent four weeks are the strongest of the engagement: the brand queries reached organic #1 and the ADA guide climbed +12.5 positions. The honest gap — and the entire case for the next six months — is that CM&D ranks for zero commercial service terms in its top 20, because the site has never had the service pages those terms require. The Portland metro searches for this work ~3,480 times a month at a blended $24 CPC (≈$84K/month in ad-equivalent value; "bathroom remodel Portland OR" alone commands a $51 CPC). The next six months at the same budget convert proven content capability + owned brand authority into booked jobs by building the 5 missing service pages, the service × suburb matrix, site-wide schema, and GA4 + GTM so lead attribution finally goes from inferred to measured.

headline.h2: Twelve weeks of work · informational footprint up · the next six months convert it to commercial ranking
headline.lede: Impressions are up +112% and the brand keyword has moved from page 3 to position 7.8. Ten blog posts targeting service-intent informational queries (walk-in shower, ADA, kitchen rebuild, insurance rebuild) are now indexed and producing impression footprint. Maps top-10 coverage spans the full 169-cell grid on the largest brand query, and the most recent four weeks are the engagement's strongest in Search Console — the brand queries reached organic #1. What hasn't been built yet are the commercial service pages those impressions should route to — and that's what the next six months are for, at the same budget.

deep_analysis.intro: In-depth read on the engagement, built from three independent data sources: Google Search Console (verified property, siteOwner access), DataForSEO Labs ranked-keywords + Google Ads search-volume (Portland-metro and national, pulled 2026-06-02), and the Local Dominator grid. The story it tells is consistent across all three: the content engine is proven and brand authority is real — and the commercial service layer that converts both into booked jobs is the part still waiting to be built.

organic_footprint.title: What CM&D actually ranks for today (the real organic footprint)
organic_footprint.summary: cmdesigns.net ranks organically for 44 keywords. The site owns its brand outright — #1 for "construction management & design," #1 for "construction management and design," #5 for "cm&d." But of its five top-20 rankings, all five are brand-name variants. There is not a single commercial service term (bathroom remodel, kitchen remodel, general contractor, walk-in shower) in CM&D's top 20. That isn't a failure — it's the whole opportunity in one number: the site has never had the service pages those terms require, so it has never been eligible to rank for them. Build the pages and the eligibility follows.
organic_footprint.interpretation: Brand control is the asset most contractors never secure and CM&D already has it. The missing piece is the commercial layer — and because nothing currently competes for that real estate from CM&D's own site, every service page built in M4-M9 enters open ground rather than fighting an incumbent CM&D page.

content_proof.title: The content engine is proven — not theoretical
content_proof.source: GSC · engagement window Mar 12 – Jun 9 2026 · page × query
content_proof.summary: Ten posts shipped in 12 weeks, and the data shows they work. Two are already on page one of Google: /post/walk-in-shower-permits-in-portland at position 7 and /post/insurance-rebuilds-in-portland at position 6. The /post/ada-walk-in-shower-requirements guide has become a genuine topical-authority asset — it ranks for a cluster of 44 distinct ADA-shower queries in GSC (accessible showers Portland, ADA shower requirements, ADA shower pan requirements, handicap shower requirements, and 40 more) and carries the largest single-page impression footprint on the site. Across the quarter, 186 brand-new search queries surfaced the site that produced zero impressions in the prior 90 days. The engine that finds and ranks content is running; what it lacks is a commercial destination to route that readership into.

local_opportunity.title: The Portland-metro prize, sized honestly
local_opportunity.source: DataForSEO · Google Ads Search Volume · location = Portland, Oregon · 2026-06-02
local_opportunity.summary: The earlier ~395K figure is US-national and overstates what a Portland contractor can actually capture — so here is the honest local number. Across 24 tracked commercial service terms (general contractor, bathroom/kitchen remodel, walk-in shower, near-me and suburb variants), the Portland metro generates roughly 3,480 searches per month. What makes this cohort valuable isn't the volume — it's the intent: the blended cost-per-click is $24, and "bathroom remodel Portland OR" alone commands a $51 CPC. Put differently, the paid-search-equivalent value of fully ranking for this local demand is on the order of $84,000 per month — that's what advertisers pay to reach these searchers, and it's the value of owning the organic positions instead. CM&D captures essentially none of it today because it has no pages backing the terms.

competitor_footprint.title: How the footprint compares to established local competitors
competitor_footprint.summary: The gap is structural, not effort-based. An established local general contractor like BnK Construction (281 reviews) ranks for 384 keywords with 38 in the top 10; L. Evans Design Group ranks for 355. CM&D ranks for 44, of which roughly 40 are brand-name variants. The difference is almost entirely the presence of built-out, schema-backed service and project pages — exactly the asset M4-M9 produces. CM&D doesn't need to out-work these competitors; it needs the page inventory they already have.

root_cause.intro: Five structural gaps that the next-6-months plan is designed to close. A1 and A2 are why we don't yet rank on the service-intent queries. A3 is the technical multiplier. A4 is why we can't yet measure leads. A5 is context.

items.title: The site does not yet back the GBP
items.body: The GBP lists 27 service items across 6 categories (Construction company · Home builder · Kitchen Renovator · Bathroom Renovator · General Contractor · Custom home builder). The site backs one of them: /kitchen-remodeling. For every other claim, Google looks for confirming relevance signals on the site and finds either a portfolio gallery (/bathrooms is 65 words with no H1) or nothing. The 10 blog posts shipped have started building authority around walk-in shower / ADA / kitchen rebuild / insurance rebuild topics — what's missing is the SERVICE PAGE PARENTS those posts should route into.

items.title: Suburb pages signal "generated content"
items.body: The nine suburb pages on the site use one of eight rotating modifiers in the URL — dependable / efficient / trusted / fast / quality (×2) / premium / local / skilled — in front of a generic service stem and "-or" suffix. The content itself is not thin (the Marylhurst page is ~950 words with specific landmarks), but the URL pattern reads as algorithmically generated, which is a known suppression trigger.

items.title: Zero schema markup anywhere
items.body: Homepage, the one service page, suburb pages, hub page — none carry LocalBusiness / GeneralContractor / Service / AreaServed JSON-LD. The Wix theme is not emitting schema and no custom code is injected. Competitors with 1-2 reviews (TS Construction, Northwest Construction, T&M Design) out-rank CMD on the brand-name queries largely because their site/profile coupling is cleaner.

items.title: No conversion tracking installed
items.body: No Google Tag Manager, no GA4, no Microsoft Clarity, no Meta Pixel detected on the homepage. The GBP website link is correctly UTM-tagged (utm_source=google&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=gbp), so a gmb_click event would fire if GA4 were listening — nothing is listening. Until tracking lands we cannot show "X leads from organic" in client-facing reporting.

items.title: Review profile below the floor of the local pack
items.body: CM&D holds 6 reviews at 5.0★. Across the top-10 competitors on these queries, the median is 26 reviews and the leader (NW Tub & Shower) carries 841. Review work is outside HQDM scope — flagging as context. At 6 reviews CM&D is below the threshold where review count starts contributing positively to ranking weight; this is a real ceiling on long-term position once everything else is fixed.

grid.intro: 13×13 grid (169 cells, 1-mile spacing) centered at (45.3642, -122.6484) — Milwaukie/Oak Grove, anchoring south Portland metro through Lake Oswego, West Linn, Oregon City and Tigard. This is exactly CM&D's GBP service area. Vertical dashed line on charts = HQDM engagement start (2026-03-12).
grid.weak_quadrant: Cells where CM&D falls fastest cluster in the northwest quadrant of the grid — the Beaverton / Tigard / Lake Oswego corridor (lat 45.38-45.45, lng -122.77 to -122.67). These are the highest-population cells; they pull more competitive results from established names. CM&D's centroid strength holds in the South Milwaukie / Oak Grove ring closer to the geocoded service area, then decays sharply toward population centers — the classic prominence/proximity signature of a profile with authority gaps that the next-6-months service × suburb matrix is designed to close.

potential.what_breaks_if_we_dont_continue: The 10 blog posts and the schema-less site keep producing impressions but stay capped at the same position bands they're in today (15-50). The walk-in-shower-permits page at position 7 is the only one currently positioned to convert; the other 9 sit too deep to drive booked jobs. The competitive group 2 (NW Tub & Shower at 841 reviews, BnK at 281) keeps gaining ground on the service-intent grid because nothing structural changes about CM&D's site. Maps brand-name top-3 stays flat instead of growing toward full-grid dominance. The investment to date stops short of the conversion point.

plan.intro: Five workstreams that map to the next 6 months. D1 and D2 unlock the rest; D3 is foundational housekeeping; D4 lets us measure; D5 is GBP surface work that's already in good shape.

workstreams.title: Service-page rebuild · the core fix
workstreams.body: Build the service pages the GBP claims and the site doesn't back. Order: P0 = /bathroom-remodeling/ + /walk-in-shower-conversion/ + /kitchen-repair/. P1 = /kitchen-remodeling/ rebuild + /general-contractor/. P2 = /fireplace-builder/, /outdoor-living-spaces/, /insurance-rebuild/, /home-addition/. Page spec: 1,200-1,500 words, Service + AreaServed schema, suburbs block linking to suburb pages, FAQ (5-7 Qs), click-to-call + email CTAs. Mirror the Marylhurst page voice — landmarks + permits — it works.

workstreams.title: Schema — LocalBusiness + Service + AreaServed
workstreams.body: JSON-LD via Wix custom code. GeneralContractor on every page with name, phone, URL, CCB #112648, WA #CONSTMD742DF, geoCircle + 8-city areaServed. Service schema per service page. BreadcrumbList on non-home pages. Validate via validator.schema.org and Rich Results Test.

M5+: add service-suffix children like /marylhurst/bathroom-remodeling/ as their parent service pages land — that's the service × suburb matrix.
